“We needed to build a team that could play in this way, could defend with resilience and playing with passion when our opponents were attacking. We needed defenders, we needed the keeper, we needed everyone committed in that direction. We needed to feel strong first, then we could try to play with our structure and our ability. This is the competitive way.”

Sports.title: Holmberg rescues point for Arsenal but Manchester United off the mark in WSL
Sports.content:
Arsenal were mightily relieved as a 95th-minute Smilla Holmberg volley rescued a point at home to a much-improved Manchester United side, but the draw will not be enough to eradicate concerns about how far behind the leaders Manchester City Renée Slegers’ team are slipping already and how frequently they seem to struggle to break down a low block.

A defiant Manchester United stunned the north Londoners as Eva Olid’s side claimed the first point of her tenure with a performance that defied all of the pre-match scripts, but it was very nearly a victory, had it not been for Holmberg’s last-gasp back-post finish from Leah Williamson’s deep, diagonal ball into the box, which finally broke the visitors’ stubborn resistance.

Widely criticised for their dismal displays in their opening two defeats against London City Lionesses and Chelsea, Manchester United were heavily tipped to struggle again at the Emirates but an encouraging defensive effort and an against-the-run-of-play Julia Zigiotti Olme strike gave them a precious lead in a display that will buy the former Hearts manager Olid plenty of time to continue working on her style on the training ground and quieten those doubting her.

Instead it will be Arsenal now facing scrutiny as they failed to win at home for a second straight game and slipped four points behind the defending champions, Manchester City, after just three rounds of fixtures. Last term, Manchester City dropped points in only four games and the early-season leaders have a 100% record so far. Arsenal’s next two WSL games are away to Chelsea and Manchester City.

“It’s not ideal, it’s not what we wanted at all, four lost points,” Slegers admitted, reflected on consecutive home draws, but she added: “It’s round three in the WSL, there are a lot of games left to play. Let’s see in May, how it ends. Not converting dominance into wins, that’s something we have to look at. We believe in the quality of the squad. When that starts clicking, it’s going to be really good.”

View image in fullscreen Manchester United’s Julia Zigiotti Olme celebrates scoring against Arsenal. Photograph: Paul Harding/WSL/WSL Football/Getty Images

In truth, this was a result that Arsenal could ill-afford, especially after last weekend’s goalless draw at home to the newly promoted side Crystal Palace, where the north Londoners were surprisingly wasteful in the final third. Slegers’ team had scored just one goal from 43 shots across their opening two league fixtures. Surely, therefore, a home match against a side who conceded five goals last time out was the perfect opportunity to banish any concerns of a lack of clinical quality in the final third? Think again.

The hosts did create good openings and looked to have control of the midfield. Their winger Lisa Baum shot straight at Phallon Tullis-Joyce early on and was providing dangerous crosses from the left. Mariona Caldentey also went close, curling just wide and Tullis-Joyce made a fine save to keep out Stina Blackstenius’ header. Nevertheless, it had been United’s Elisabeth Terland who went closest in the first half, being thwarted by two excellent Misa Rodríguez saves in quick succession.

View image in fullscreen Phallon Tullis-Joyce leaping up to make a crucial save to keep Arsenal at bay. Photograph: Nina Farooqi/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock

Arsenal stepped up the pressure after half-time but Georgia Stanway – one of Arsenal’s better performers for the rest of the game – made a costly error as she tried to play a simple pass back towards the centre-back Steph Catley that carelessly rolled the ball into the path of Zigiotti Olme instead. The grateful Manchester United midfielder confidently stepped the ball around Catley and slotted through the legs of Rodríguez. The Emirates was astonished. The United bench, jubilant.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

From then on, it was ‘backs to the wall’ for the visitors, much like it was during the majority of this fixture last term, which ended goalless. Tullis-Joyce dived low and strong to keep out a Cailtin Foord effort and United battled well to clear the danger from several set pieces as the home side grew increasingly frustrated. The crowd eventually erupted as the substitute Holmberg earned them a point and Manchester United’s players fell to their knees.

Quick Guide WSL roundup: Chelsea's Potter and Malard sink Birmingham Show Chelsea and London City Lionesses climbed the Women’s Super League table with respective victories over Birmingham and Charlton. After thumping Manchester United 5-0 last weekend, Chelsea won again as Lexi Potter and Melvine Malard secured a 2-0 win. Potter found the roof of the net in the eighth minute (the celebrations pictured above) and in the 71st minute the France star Malard made a quick impact from the bench with her first goal at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea moved up to second and with their goal difference were likely to stay there. London City lost 2-1 to West Ham last time out but impressed in a 4-1 triumph at promoted Charlton. Isobel Goodwin’s double had London City two goals ahead after 15 minutes and, despite Jodie Hutton halving the deficit in the 39th minute with a fine finish, Jana Fernández restored their advantage before half-time. The German forward Nicole Anyomi made sure the outcome was no longer in doubt with the Lionesses’ fourth after 76 minutes. They sit third, a point behind Chelsea. Press Association Photograph: Yaroslav Dunka/Shutterstock Editorial Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Olid was pleased with their display, though, explaining: “After losing 5-0, the focus this week was the defensive shape, because I think the attack will come. Implementing a new style of play needs time. But the effort, the hard work, the intensity, that can never be missing. It was so important to see that today. That is the minimum. Now, from here, little-by-little, we will improve the attacking style.”

Sports.title: Coventry delight in Jay Dasilva winner but ruled-out goal riles Nottingham Forest
Sports.content:
No, but seriously. Maybe Frank Lampard and Coventry can achieve Premier League survival. The club’s first top-division win since April 2001 was celebrated rapturously, victory an object lesson in unsettling opponents for whom confidence can waver. Jay Dasilva’s excellent goal was built on the foundations laid by a battling defensive performance that must be replicated on a weekly basis. Coventry, dogged throughout, blunted Nottingham Forest’s creativity, though could thank a late video assistant referee call that enraged the City Ground crowd.

Lampard declared, with his broadest grin: “I feel great, I feel amazing.” Next, as is his way, back to serious business. “The reality in football is you have to fight for it, you have to work for it, you have to have organisation.”

Coventry’s troubled start to the season had revived doubts in his capabilities as a Premier League manager and far too many echoes of a quarter century in the wilderness. Whatever happens, their fans, under the weakening, early-evening sun, were determined to enjoy themselves. Even if it’s for a single season, why not make the most of things? “Something we have to build on and not get too carried away,” said Bobby Thomas, having personified that rearguard effort.

“We are a team with a lot of players having their first stint in Premier League football,” said Lampard. “Not everyone is a Wayne Rooney or a superstar that can just own it.”

Forest’s home league record in 2026 continues to be wretched: only Burnley, in April, have left in defeat. The previous week’s victory at Aston Villa offered further confirmation of Morgan Gibbs-White’s importance to Forest, as if it were needed. He remains ignored by Thomas Tuchel despite verifiable claims of being the most in-form English No 10 around, only Pascal Gross creating more chances in the Premier League this season, though like his team as a whole, Gibbs-White is doing his best work away from West Bridgford. Forest hit 26 shots on Coventry’s goal, just three on target.

View image in fullscreen Jay Dasilva fires home Coventry’s 55th-minute winner. Photograph: David Klein/Reuters

“We struggled with scoring,” was Oliver Glasner’s simple diagnosis. “Today was the first time I could feel the heaviness of the past, it was very quiet in the dressing room. When we conceded the goal, everyone was nervous, the entire ground was nervous and I think the reason is last year.”

An early deft header to Liam Delap and a cogent flick to James McAtee had suggested Gibbs-White was in the mood but Forest never found the momentum to crack Coventry’s defensive shield. McAtee’s talents have never quite found their position but playing deeper as Gibbs-White’s creative partner has suited him. However, the duo were far less in tune than the previous week. Delap has shown signs of being the player glimpsed at Ipswich but was another lost in heavy traffic, Forest reduced to potshots such as his snapshot wide.

Quick Guide Nottingham Forest 0-1 Coventry key facts Show • Coventry earned their first Premier League victory of the season – it’s their 100th win in the competition overall, and first since April 2001 (1-0 v Sunderland). • Jay Dasilva scored Coventry’s first Premier League goal of the season. Assisted by Carl Rushworth, it’s just the second time a team’s first goal in a campaign has been assisted by a goalkeeper, after Peter Schmeichel for Manchester United in 1992-93. • Nottingham Forest have failed to score in their first three home games in a league campaign for the first time in their history. Opta Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Coventry’s kick-off for the second half saw their players line up in a formation resembling that for a rugby union dropout. It achieved little but previewed the long-ball tactics that brought about the breaking of their 25-year duck.

Loum Tchaouna, a half-time arrival, cutting inside to shoot, if too weakly to beat Matz Sels, might have served as a further warning to Forest, as within moments, Dasilva, showing admirable strength for someone of such diminutive dimensions and a beautiful first touch to beat Daniel Muñoz, blazed to a diagonal ball from his goalkeeper, Carl Rushworth. The finish was just as adept, the celebrations deafening. Coventry’s previous Premier League scorer had been Mustapha Hadji in a losing effort at Aston Villa that confirmed relegation.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen The big screen shows Igor Jesus has been deemed to have fouled Caleb Yirenkyi on review. Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA

For an increasingly ragged Forest, Chris Wood, old reliable, was thrown on, as was Igor Jesus, with Delap pushed to the wings. If anything, that led to Forest losing their shape and poise further, even if chances came. Thomas dashed back to the goalline to clear a chip from Igor Jesus that had Rushworth beaten.

Igor Jesus did get the ball in the net, only for the video assistant referee to advise Jarred Gillett that Caleb Yirenkyi had been fouled, and the on-pitch official agreed. It looked harsh: Yirenkyi had fallen readily under minimal contact. “I was worried,” Lampard said.

A shrugging Glasner said: “The referee decided and we accept it, that’s it.” Forest fans have had more than their fill of video-assisted officiating. Their seething, guttural rage came by contrast to Coventry fans now able to savour the Premier League ride.

Sports.title: Zidane’s next move as France coach may reveal the wizard behind the curtain | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
Even in his playing days, Zinedine Zidane seemed unknowable. As a manager, the sense of distance has only grown. He won three Champions Leagues with Real Madrid without ever giving a sense of what his idea of football looked like.

France are perhaps the most perplexing football country: a squad that teems with such talent that a B team would be serious contenders at a World Cup, that reached three major finals under Didier Deschamps with a sense of unfulfilment, a team that progressed but rarely entranced, or at least didn’t until this summer’s World Cup, when they attacked with gusto and ended up overrun in midfield by Spain.

On Friday, the two come together as Zidane, for the first time, leads France in their Nations League fixture against Turkey, an enigmatic coach leading a mercurial squad.

Zidane is one of five coaches to have won the Champions League on three or more occasions, ranking alongside Bob Paisley, Pep Guardiola and Luis Enrique and behind only Carlo Ancelotti. He is the only manager to win three successive Champions Leagues and yet few would consider him one of the game’s elite coaches. In that spell he won one La Liga title.

He left five days after the third of those Champions League successes, vaguely citing the club’s need for change. Like so much else in his career, his motivations were opaque. But he returned the following March after the inglorious reign of Julen Lopetegui and Santi Solari’s attempt to pick up the pieces. He won another La Liga title in the two full seasons that followed.

How to assess a coach in the modern world? Two league titles in four full seasons. Three Champions Leagues in his first two and a half seasons. In another age, in another country, that would have marked Zidane as indisputably elite, but in Spain in the past decade? Domestically, his achievements feel about par.

View image in fullscreen Zinedine Zidane was viewed at Real Madrid as a head coach who let his star players like Ronaldo and Gareth Bale just be. Photograph: Matt West/BPI/Shutterstock

Madrid and Barcelona win everything, so for a Madrid coach to win half the league titles available is essentially what would be expected. But he lost eight of his first 100 games, a record. His side scored in a record 73 consecutive games. They won a joint-record 16 La Liga games in a row. They won a record 13 successive away games.

They are stats that seem unanswerable, but their accumulation has the opposite effect to that which might be expected. Zidane’s Madrid, in his first spell, were crushingly dominant. But were they dominant because of his genius or did he appear a genius because of their dominance? What comes to matter, then, is not the how many, but the how. Did Madrid win with dashing football of fitting elegance? To which the answer is, again, a shrug: they were fine.

Those three Champions League wins in a row, equally, offer surprisingly little evidence for Zidane’s greatness. Madrid have always had a tremendous capacity for achieving European success in the shadows, as though they are the default, the club that wins when nobody else is quite inspired enough to do so. Rarely has that been felt as acutely as in 2016, when they beat Roma and Wolfsburg, then edged by Manchester City on penalties in the semi-final thanks to a Fernando own goal before beating Atlético Madrid on penalties in an unmemorable final.

The following year was more impressive: the extra-time surge against Bayern and Cristiano Ronaldo-inspired demolitions of Napoli, Atlético and Juventus. But 2018 was a return to curiously ordinary success. Yes, Ronaldo and Luka Modrić were often brilliant, but there was also carelessness, notably in the quarter-final win against Juventus when they let a three-goal lead slip before a late penalty rescued them. Victory over Liverpool in the final came after a shoulder injury sustained by Mohamed Salah in a challenge with Sergio Ramos, a terrible error by a possibly injured Loris Karius and a Gareth Bale wonder goal.

View image in fullscreen Didier Deschamps was successful as head coach of France, but his side rarely captivated Photograph: Martin Meissner/AP

It was hard to isolate any one moment in the success that could definitively be assigned to Zidane’s coaching genius. He didn’t create the midfield three of Casemiro, Modric and Toni Kroos. He didn’t find some new role for Ronaldo or Bale. Perhaps Zidane was some elite player whisperer, coaxing them to habitual greatness, but it was hard for an outsider to tell. Being Zidane, he was inscrutable, a cipher into which observers could read whatever message they wished.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Real Madrid coaches often run into a similar problem. They have great players. Great players do great things. Philosophies and structures always seem subservient to their talents. Ancelotti, like Zidane, has often been underappreciated, seen as somebody who essentially lets the players be. That is probably unfair and, even if it were not, perhaps that, too, is a skill. After all, plenty of coaches at Real Madrid have not been able to let the players express their innate superiority.

At the very least, it can be said that Zidane has an aura. Even those who accused him of being little more than a pair of hands clapping on the touchline must acknowledge that some hands are more authoritative than others. That may turn out to be an essential quality with France, a national team that became notorious between their two World Cup triumphs for ill-discipline, with the scandals of Seoul in 2002 and the strike at Knysna in 2010.

Whatever doubts there may be about whether Deschamps’s caution was counterproductive – until at the last, in that semi-final against Spain, he wasn’t cautious enough – over his 14 years in charge he prevented the sort of breakdowns of discipline that had undermined his predecessors, despite some extremely challenging situations.

Perhaps this is not such a troubled or troublesome France squad as some of the past decade have been, but that Zidane has taken the unusual step of banning the press from covering the arrival of players at their Clairefontaine base suggests he is eager to make a bid for control early.

His squad features a number of new faces. This is not continuity Deschamps. In the greater autonomy national coaches have compared with their club counterparts, perhaps, with France, the true nature of Zidane the coach will emerge and the great enigma will develop a face.

Sports.title: Everton hold off Ipswich thanks to Thierno Barry goal despite VAR controversy
Sports.content:
After the trials and tribulations of the transfer window, Everton can be content with fifth place, an unbeaten start and five clean sheets in seven games. There will also be relief, for Pro Ref as well as David Moyes, that another controversial call from a video assistant referee did not impede their progress against Ipswich.

Thierno Barry decided a close-fought contest with his fifth goal of the campaign. He should have had a sixth but an offside Brennan Johnson was adjudged to have impacted Ipswich goalkeeper Christian Walton’s ability to save a ball he made no attempt to save and was nowhere near saving. Unlike last weekend’s Manchester derby, however, referee Stuart Attwell’s decision would not prove decisive. The game turned in Everton’s favour minutes later when Abdul Fatawu received a second yellow card for diving but, having failed to kill off Gary O’Neil’s 10 men, they ended up hanging on. VAR was therefore spared Moyes’s wrath.

“They said it affected his ability to save it which I don’t think was the case,” said the Everton manager, far more relaxed than he would have been had Ipswich levelled late on. “It’s really difficult for referees, we understand that. Do I think we will get consistency from that decision through all the season on the same thing? I’ll be doubtful of that. There is no doubt Brennan was offside but did he really interfere, was the goalkeeper ever going to save it?”

O’Neil took a differing view, and also claimed his visitors controlled the game. That was stretching it. Everton were extremely careless in possession with the usually reliable Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, Jarrad Branthwaite, James Garner and Harrison Armstrong among those responsible. But they created enough chances to have rendered Ipswich’s stirring finale irrelevant, 21 in total, though managed only two on target. “I am ratting the players like you wouldn’t believe,” added Moyes. “Why are we not scoring more? I think that’s one of the things we are missing from being a half-decent side.”

Johnson missed a gilt-edged chance from an Armstrong pass before Barry delivered an early lead with his strangest goal of the season. The striker reacted sharply to divert James Tarkowski’s 25-yard volley into the net after Walton and the lively Jack Clarke had cleared a cross from Dewsbury-Hall. The Ipswich keeper had Tarkowski’s shot covered only for Barry to leave him wrong-footed by chesting the ball into the opposite side of the goal. The striker clearly moved to play the ball with his chest, so gets the benefit of the doubt over his intention.

Fatawu was a persistent threat down Ipswich’s right flank, making his dismissal all the more galling for O’Neil as his team chased an equaliser. The Ghana international forced a fine save from Jordan Pickford after Everton made a hash of clearing his corner and attempted to beat the England goalkeeper from inside his own half. The long-range effort was drifting wide but Pickford, unawares, took no chances and scampered back to save. Fatawu should also have claimed an assist when floating a cross over the Everton defence to Leif Davis. The left-back, perhaps surprised to find himself onside and unmarked in front of goal, scuffed his shot badly wide of the far post.

View image in fullscreen Stuart Attwell shows Ipswich’s Abdul Fatawu (centre) a second yellow card for simulation. Photograph: Alex Dodd/Shutterstock

Ipswich started the second half on top with Pickford saving from Julio Enciso and Abdoul Ouattara in quick succession. But it was Everton who converted next when Barry rose between four static Ipswich players and headed Dewsbury-Hall’s corner in off the far post. Walton was nowhere near the ball and did not appeal any infringement by the offside Johnson. Referee Attwell, sent to the pitch-side monitor, infuriated the home crowd by disallowing the goal on the basis Johnson was offside and affecting the keeper’s ability to save the ball.

Fatawu foolishly helped Everton recover. Booked for hauling down Dewsbury-Hall in the first half, the winger invited a second yellow card when diving to win a free-kick against Garner. He became only the third player in the last six Premier League seasons to receive a second yellow card for simulation.

Everton had numerous chances against Ipswich’s ten men but Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall and Armstrong all miscued while Walton produced a fine save to deny impressive substitute Tyler Dibling. Their profligacy made for a nervy finale as the visitors piled forward in search of an equaliser. Branthwaite, launching himself in the way of Diop’s goal-bound shot, helped Everton over the line.

Sports.title: Newcastle back to winning ways as Willock and Hall end Hull’s unbeaten start
Sports.content:
Hull always knew, sooner or later, they would lose a Premier League game, but no one can say they did not do everything in their power to try to delay that inaugural top-tier defeat.

After conceding two goals in the opening seven minutes, Hull could easily have folded but they are made of sterner stuff than that. Tellingly, they also sensed the inherent fragility of a gifted, but injury-hit and extremely youthful Newcastle.

Once Matthias Jaissle was forced into a late switch to an unloved three at the back and Mohamed-Ali Cho narrowed the scoreline, the visitors assumed control and it almost seemed a minor miracle that Newcastle clung on for a morale-boosting victory.

“I’m very proud of how we played this game, especially the second half,” said Sergej Jakirovic. “We made mistakes in the first 10 minutes and Newcastle were clinical on the counterattack, but after that, I think we showed our mentality and our character. Over 90 minutes, we deserved a point. My team showed they will not be beaten easily.”

Jaissle had harsh words for his players after Monday’s 4-1 defeat at Leeds and it seemed they had the desired effect. Sure enough, Joe Willock swiftly lashed the ball beyond Konstantinos Tzolakis. Three minutes were on the clock and it was only the third goal Hull’s £20m Greece goalkeeper had conceded since arriving from Olympiakos.

It came after John Egan blocked Willock’s initial shot, but Hull’s subsequent failure to clear permitted Harvey Barnes to pick out the midfielder.

Four minutes later, Barnes was once again the creator as he exchanged passes with the excellent Lewis Hall before the left-back, recalled to the England squad on Friday, swept the crispest of shots low into the bottom-left corner. Significantly, it had all begun with Hall dispossessing Oli McBurnie deep in Newcastle’s half.

Tino Livramento, too, was included in Thomas Tuchel’s latest squad, but the right-back’s chances of joining up with England receded when an injury collected in training ruled him out here. Livramento was one of nine home absentees, but, undeterred, a youthful starting XI initially delighted in a spot of tiger taming.

As much as Hull struggled to second-guess the dynamic Willock and the impressive 18-year-old Sean Steur in the home midfield, they were not subdued entirely. Hull came close to reducing the deficit when Sorba Thomas almost turned in a Matt Crooks cross at the near post.

When, deep in first-half stoppage time, Thomas slipped before pulling the advancing Jacob Murphy back by an ankle, a penalty was awarded. Yoane Wissa stepped up, but his rather under-powered kick was saved by Tzolakis.

View image in fullscreen Joe Willock slots Newcastle into a third-minute lead from close range. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters

Newcastle’s substitutes featured five academy players including the winger Kyran Thompson, a first year scholar who left school this summer, but when, midway through the second half, Jaissleturned to his bench he introduced the 34-year-old Fabian Schär in place of a tiring Steur.

This change prompted a switch to a back three, featuring Schär at its heart. That configuration is, as Jaissle has made abundantly clear, far from his favourite formation and that feeling probably crystallised when, almost immediately, Hull scored.

Cho’s goal was created when Lewis Miley – relocated from right-back to midfield – was caught in possession, enabling Mohamed Belloumi to play in the summer signing from Nice. Cho, a former England youth international turned France Under-21 forward, duly revelled in whipping a close-range left-foot shot past Lukas Hornicek.

From then on Hull blitzed Newcastle’s area with a barrage of crosses, corners and shots from all angles. Newcastle were under siege and, among assorted other saves, their goalkeeper did particularly well to extend a foot and somehow divert Robinio Vaz’s half-volley.

“It was an intense game,” said Jaissle, whose backroom staff exchanged words with their Hull counterparts. “We started at a really high level, it was the right reaction to Leeds. But the missed penalty changed momentum. We tired and we needed to suffer, but the commitment to win this game was exceptional. It made me proud. It was something special.”

Sports.title: European football: Martínez double gives Inter comeback draw at Roma
Sports.content:
Lautaro Martínez rode to Inter’s rescue as the Serie A champions fought back from 2-0 down to force a 2-2 draw at Roma, in a meeting of what had been the last two sides with 100% records.

Manu Koné’s double had given Roma a 2-0 lead at half-time but for the second time in a week Cristian Chivu’s side, inspired by Martínez, showed mettle as the champions fought back from such a deficit.

After the announcement earlier in the day of the death of Sandro Mazzola at the age of 83, both sides paid homage to the former Inter and Italy playmaker prior to kick-off, with the Nerazzurri also sporting black armbands.

Roma raced out of the blocks as Koné sent them ahead with less than six minutes on the clock when he readjusted his body well to rifle home Nahuel Molina’s knockdown.

View image in fullscreen Roma supporters hold up scarves during their match against Inter. Photograph: Ciro De Luca/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

The champions had bounced back from being 2-0 down inside the opening 16 minutes at home to Udinese to emerge 5-3 winners on Monday. But Inter were not at the races for most of the opening period at the Stadio Olimpico as Paulo Dybala twice threatened to double the hosts’ advantage.

However, just as Inter slowly seemed to be waking up, Koné had the ball in the net again when he tucked in from close range at the back post on 37 minutes. His celebrations were initially cut short by the assistant’s flag before the video assistant referee intervened and, after a lengthy review, Davide Massa pointed to the centre circle as the 25-year-old skipped off in delight after notching the sixth Serie A goal of his career.

Martínez halved the deficit less than a minute after the interval with a scuffed finish from Thuram’s pull-back that just crept perfectly into the side-netting of Mile Svilar’s far post.

Just as the match appeared to be petering out going into the final 10 minutes, a sudden goalmouth scramble saw Svilar make a sharp save before Martínez headed on to the bar under pressure. Inter, however, managed to recycle the ball and it came back to the Argentinian inside the box and this time he made no mistake as he controlled with his thigh and arrowed a finish past the Serb to ensure the spoils were shared.

Lazio joined their city rivals Roma and Inter on 13 points after beating bottom-side Venezia, who remain pointless, 2-0. A 51st-minute Mattia Zaccagni penalty, coupled with a Tijjani Noslin goal on the hour, was enough to earn Gennaro Gattuso’s team a fourth win from five outings.

Paris FC extended their unbeaten start to the Ligue 1 campaign, beating Liam Rosenior’s old charges Strasbourg 2-1 in a match marred by abusive chants towards the Englishman from visiting fans.

View image in fullscreen Liam Rosenior raises his arms in jubilation to celebrate victory in front of the Strasbourg supporters. Photograph: Matthieu Mirville/DPPI/Shutterstock

The game was halted in the second half as Rosenior was targeted by his former supporters. There were also ugly scenes after the final whistle as Rosenior motioned to remonstrate with the away fans and had to be pulled away by his players.

He said later: “A small section of the fans, and I want to stress that it was only a small section, because Strasbourg is a fantastic club, were disrespectful. They insulted my family. My bench was very angry. So, for me, celebrating like that was obviously sending a message. I won’t say anything more about this.”

Goals from Ilan Kebbal on 18 minutes and Pablo Pagis 12 minutes into the second half were enough for the capital club to add a third win to their two draws so far this campaign, despite conceding a late own goal by Moustapha Mbow.

The game between Lyon and ⁠Stade Rennais was also disrupted after ⁠Lyon ​fans ‌displayed an ‌offensive banner ‌directed at their rivals St Etienne. Lyon were leading 2-0 ‌through two goals from ​Ernest Nuamah when the banner ⁠was unveiled, prompting ​officials to ​suspend ​the match ​briefly ‌before ​play ​resumed. They went on to win 4-0.

Barcelona maintained their ⁠100% record this season with a 3-1 La Liga ⁠victory over Sevilla, as captain Raphinha scored a hat-trick ⁠to continue his remarkable start to the campaign. Sevilla opened ⁠the scoring after 18 minutes ​through a ‌Youssouf Fofana header, ‌but Barcelona hit back with ‌a Raphinha strike four minutes later.

Seven minutes into the second half, Raphinha headed in a Lamine Yamal cross and the pair combined again ​as the Brazilian completed his hat-trick in the 69th minute, his 12th league goal in ⁠seven games this season. Barcelona are ​provisionally ​six points clear ​at the top of ​La Liga, with ‌second-placed Real ​Madrid, ​who have a game in hand, playing Atlético Madrid on Sunday.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Maximilian Beier’s 70th-minute winner secured Borussia Dortmund a 1-0 victory at Stuttgart as they moved to the top of the early Bundesliga table. Beier tapped in from Jobe Bellingham’s low cross to send Dortmund to the summit for the first time since May 2023, a run of 1,212 days since they threw away the title with a final-day home draw against Mainz.

View image in fullscreen Maximilian Beier (centre) celebrates with teammates after scoring Borussia Dortmund’s winner against VfB Stuttgart. Photograph: Ronald Wittek/EPA

The victory also marks the first time in a decade Dortmund have won their opening four league matches. “Sounds good to me,” Beier told Sky Germany. “We’ll take that.”

Earlier, Freiburg had missed a chance to return to the top of the Bundesliga after being held to a 2-2 draw at Eintracht Frankfurt. Bayern Munich’s ruthless 7-0 win over Union Berlin on Friday had put them top overnight.

Several new members of Jürgen Klopp’s 44-man Germany squad shone on both sides in a see-sawing encounter. Frankfurt’s Younes Ebnoutalib finished off a lovely team move to score 10 minutes in, two days after a surprise first call-up.

Derry Scherhant, another of Klopp’s lesser-known new additions, levelled for Freiburg, but Jonathan Burkardt edged Frankfurt back in front. Scherhant created a second for Yuito Suzuki to grab Freiburg a point and leave them level with Bayern on 10 points.

Mohamed Salah scored a hat-trick and set up another ⁠goal as Trabzonspor thrashed Galatasaray 4-0, handing the ⁠defending champions their first defeat of the Turkish Super Lig season.

Salah opened ⁠the scoring in the fourth minute, running through from midfield and finishing calmly, ⁠before he turned provider to set up Noah ​Saviolo, who struck ‌from inside ‌the penalty area in the 39th. Salah added a ‌third in the 44th minute with a clinical finish from a Franculino Dju assist. He completed his ‌hat-trick in the 80th minute, running more than half the length of the ​pitch unchallenged to score with a trademark side-foot finish.

Galatasaray’s coach, Okan Buruk, was sent to the stands in the 71st minute while Lesley ⁠Ugochukwu was shown a red card in the ​87th. Trabzonspor are fifth in the table with 10 points from six games, three points behind Galatasaray.

Sports.title: Bill Belichick blasted for rude interview with sideline reporter... as girlfriend Jordon Hudson joins him after controversial week for his UNC team
Sports.content:
Bill Belichick blasted for rude interview with sideline reporter... as girlfriend Jordon Hudson joins him after controversial week for his UNC team

North Carolina head coach Bill Belichick sure hasn't lost his fastball - or rather, his eephus pitch - when it comes to in-game interviews.

Belichick and his Tar Heels ventured south for a battle with neighboring-state rivals Clemson in an ACC battle.

Coming out of halftime, Belichick was pulled by ESPN sideline reporter Stormy Buonantony to get his thoughts on how the first half played out.

In typical Belichickian fashion, the coach wasn't willing to give much detail and provided only the bare minimum of responses.

When asked about the penalties his team was charged with, Belichick simply replied, 'Too many, yeah. Too many.'

Buonantony tried getting more out of him and asked if there was anything else the Tar Heels needed to improve on.

College football fans criticized Bill Belichick for his terse interview with a sideline reporter

Belichick and the Tar Heels were in South Carolina to take on ACC rivals Clemson

But his halftime discussion with reporter Stormy Buonantony resulted in short answers

Belichick didn't take the bait: 'No, just gotta keep executing better. Too many penalties.'

Play-by-play man Bob Wischusen chuckled and welcomed Buonantony to 'the club' of reporters who couldn't get much out of the eight-time Super Bowl champion.

Wischusen asked how Buonantony was faring, to which she joked: 'I'm fine, I made it out alive guys.'

Football fans criticized Belichick for his terse demeanor and short responses.

'His act has grown tired and stale, he’s just an old douche now,' read one comment on X.

A similar message read, 'Just can’t help himself from being an absolute douche.'

'I feel for @StormBuonantony! But damn if she didn't handle this perfectly. Tip of the cap, ma'am!' one commenter said.

Belichick's girlfriend, Jordon Hudson, joined him for the trip across the border from North Carolina to South Carolina and wore appropriate colors for the situation.

Belichick was seen entering the stadium alongside his young girlfriend, Jordon Hudson

Hudson was spotted wearing a strapless top and long-legged pants - both in Carolina blue.

She rounded out the outfit wearing white high heels and accessorized with a white bag. Hudson also appeared to be carrying a laptop with her inside the stadium.

She was seen walking into the stadium with Belichick, who hoped to get revenge for a loss to Dabo Swinney's Clemson Tigers from last season.

Her moral support comes amid a week of controversy and change for the Tar Heels after Belichick's son, Steve Belichick, left his post as the team's defensive coordinator following an investigation into the football program's culture found 'a disregard for Carolina's values and standards of conduct.'

The 39-year-old was mysteriously placed on medical leave last month before a bombshell report from WRAL claimed investigators were looking into whether the defensive coordinator used drugs on the job or supplied drugs to at least one Tar Heels player.

The game between Clemson and North Carolina is in the middle of a lengthy weather delay due to lightning at the time of reporting. Before the pause, UNC was leading 17-15.

Sports.title: Bizarre moment former Premier League star is RUN OVER by a pitch rolling machine at half-time during match in Thailand
Sports.content:
Former Tottenham and Everton winger Andros Townsend was bizarrely run over by a roller as he was warming up for a game in Thailand. The ex-England man-turned pundit, 35, is plying his trade in the Far East, having joined PT Prachuap in the summer transfer window. Over the break, he was in the United States covering the World Cup for ITV, and made headlines for some of his diet choices during the tournament. Incredibly, though, on Saturday, he narrowly avoided serious injury when he found himself under a pitch roller while he warmed up at half-time. Footage showed the driver of the roller struggling to control the vehicle, with Townsend kicking a ball away, not looking in that direction, and the crowd gasped. The roller then hit Townsend, and he fell to the floor, with the roller literally going over his legs and lower body. 🚨Andros Townsend got lucky to avoid injury during warmups in the Thai League pic.twitter.com/ctEOycMZcF — Polymarket Sports (@PolymarketSport) September 19, 2026 Andros Townsend was bizarrely run over while warming up for a game in Thailand on Saturday Townsend went viral during the World Cup for his bizarre diet, which includes eating raw meat Incredibly, he walked away unharmed, and came on as a substitute late on in his side's 3-0 win. He would later share a video of the incident to his Instagram page. PT Prachuap – based in Prachuap Khiri Khan province, 150 miles south of Bangkok – appeared to have leaked Townsend's arrival two weeks before he joined when they asked if anyone had a three-bedroom house available for the player to live in. They are the 17th club of his career. Townsend made 29 appearances for Kanchanaburi Power last season, scoring three goals. He has previously played for Spurs, Newcastle, Palace and Everton, and moved to Thailand after a short spell with Turkish side Antalyaspor. Townsend making the move comes after he worked for ITV as a co-commentator during the World Cup. The ex-England winger went viral at the tournament for his unconventional diet – which includes eating raw steak. He released a slew of videos promoting his all-natural diet including the steak, sardines and boiled eggs on a plane. Townsend's aim was to stay healthy while staying in hotels throughout the tournament, while being denied access to cooking facilities and facing the constant temptation of fast food. 'Never let your circumstances dictate your health,' he says. Townsend claims to have been eating raw meat for four years, dating back to his time when he was in the Premier League and would have had access to industry-leading dietary advice.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi TEARS into Spurs flops after defeat by Aston Villa and sends warning to struggling stars after £320m summer splurge
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi let rip at his Tottenham flops after crashing to another home defeat which will leave them marooned in the drop zone for the next three weeks.

Spurs were 3-0 down in the 86th minute and Aston Villa had threatened to stretch further ahead before salvaging a little respectability with two late goals.

They are winless in the first five games of the Premier League season and De Zerbi did not try to hide his emotions.

He hit out at his team’s defensive ‘fragility’ and the feeble manner of Villa’s goals, especially the ‘unacceptable’ second, scored on the break by Nicolas Jackson at the start of the second half.

He demanded more strength in adversity and more from certain individuals including Dominic Solanke and Mateus Fernandes, who was replaced at half time.

He also grumbled about the problems in the transfer window.

Roberto De Zerbi hit out at his team’s defensive ‘fragility’ and the feeble manner of Villa’s goals

'I was very disappointed, very sad, very frustrated for the performance,' fumed De Zerbi. 'We can’t lose this game in this way, absolutely. We can’t concede the second goal. We can’t lose balance. In the beginning of the second half I spoke with the four attackers, to use their heads, be calm.

'It was minute 51. All the second half, be calm, play, enjoy, don’t take risks. But the goal we conceded, the second goal was incredible.'

De Zerbi was no happier about the opener, scored by Johan Manzambi when Spurs were down to 10 men because Micky van de Ven was off having treatment on a facial cut after a clash of heads with Tyrone Mings.

'I don’t want to speak about the first half when we dominated and created more chances to score,' said De Zerbi. 'My focus is on why we concede the first goal with 10 players, just for one minute in that situation.

'We can stay stronger, we can communicate more, we can defend in a compact way. I put [Rodrigo] Bentancur to centre back and Mateus Fernandes into midfield. If we have a red card we could play for 60 minutes with 10 players, so what is the problem?'

Spurs thought sub Kudus had levelled at 1-1 but the goal was ruled out by a VAR offside call and soon afterwards were 2-0 down.

'I don’t know if some players lost energy, but we conceded an unacceptable goal from a long goal kick, with a long ball,' said De Zerbi. 'We knew Aston Villa are playing 86 per cent more long balls than last season. We spoke about it in many meetings.

Spurs were 3-0 down in the 86th minute and Aston Villa had threatened to stretch further ahead before salvaging a little respectability with two late goals

'Then we have to explain another game like Newcastle, where we play well in the first half and then lose. For sure it’s an aspect.

'It’s my responsibility, I don’t want to leave without taking my responsibility, but in that moment of the game, when the game is different to ball possession, to playing in the last third, because we can’t play for 90 minutes in the last third like the first half, because there is an opponent.

'Aston Villa is not such a bad team. It is a good team, good players and the moment we have to defend, we have to defend compact. The leaders have to be leaders and lead the team.'

'Football is like life, either you are stronger or you lose.'

De Zerbi vowed also to work harder and improve but accused his players of losing their way when things conspired against them.

'In the second half, we lost balance because we were losing,' said the Spurs boss. 'We forced the pass, forced the situation, lost the ball.'

De Zerbi dropped Mathys Tel for what he called ‘technical reasons’, and demanded more from individuals including £85million summer signing Fernandes and Solanke.

On Fernandes, he said: 'I have a big confidence in Mateus, but I didn’t like his performance. Otherwise, I wouldn't change. He knows, but it’s normal, it’s not an attack on Mateus, I love Mateus, but we need more from Mateus.'

On Solanke, he said: 'We need more from him, for sure. I like Dom as a player, and I stay with him until the end. He needs to stay better, to feel better. The physical condition is not good enough.

'Maybe he doesn’t have enough confidence in himself in this moment, because he’s much better than this. But maybe many things can be better. We can’t say everything is bad, but it’s not enough.'

On summer transfers and the failure to land a reliable goalscorer, De Zerbi said: 'The transfer market was long, and the situation changed many times. There was also the Financial Fair Play to respect at the end of the transfer market.

'We didn’t sell the players we thought, in the beginning, there was the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. The club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.'

Spurs will return after the international break with a trip to Manchester United.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta fumes at Arsenal stars after 3-0 thumping by Brighton: Gunners boss warns defeat was a 'big lesson' as Bruno Guimaraes reveals angry response in dressing room after 'unacceptable' display
Sports.content:
An upset Mikel Arteta branded Brighton's pummelling of Arsenal as a 'big lesson' which had left him 'extremely disappointed' with his players on a shock afternoon for the reigning Premier League champions.

Goals from Pascal Gross and Charalampos Koustoulas put the Seagulls ahead by half-time, before Chema Andres' header added the gloss on an emphatic display.

The Gunners had been dominated from the start, leaving Arteta furious over his team's performance. It ends their seven-game unbeaten run across all competitions, and is Arsenal's first league defeat since last April against Manchester City.

Arteta said: 'Extremely disappointed, but first of all, I think we have to congratulate Brighton for the victory. I think they deserve it, they were the better team.

'Brighton were another gear up from us. We were extremely poor technically and not respecting the game.

'And from our side there were certain basics that you need to accomplish in football, especially in the Premier League, that we were very far from.

Mikel Arteta said he was 'extremely disappointed' after Arsenal were beaten 3-0 by Brighton

Arteta admitted he had a negative feeling early on in the game in an abject display from his side

'In the first duel, the second ball, that put the game, especially how direct they were, in a really difficult place for us.

'On top of that, when we did regain the ball, especially in our own half, the amount of technical errors that we did and we didn't respect any principle of play that you have to get out of those man-to-man situations.

'That put us always on the back foot, so it was very difficult to control the game. When we had moments of dominance and control, we opened them up, but we didn't finish those actions with the quality that is required.

'So at the end of the day, I think they deserve to win the game and it's a big lesson for us.'

Bruno Guimaraes was also left angry about the display and said players were complaining about it in the changing room.

'I think today is a day to forget,' said Guimaraes. 'Everything we tried didn't work. Credit to them (Brighton) as well but we can't accept this here.

'I think in the changing room, everyone was complaining about ourselves, about the level we played today. Like I said, it's not acceptable. A very bad day in the office.'

Arteta admitted he had a negative feeling about the upcoming result from the very start of the game.

'From the first throw-in you could sense it, it was so clear,' he said.

'We put ourselves in trouble one time, two times, three times and we need to get out of that much quicker than that. That's one of the biggest lessons that we have to take from the game today.'

Meanwhile, an elated Hurzeler was full of praise for his Brighton team.

He said: 'It was a special win. Not only because we played the best team in England but because of the performance. I am really proud of my team. It's always important to enjoy these moments. We were horrible to play against.'

Asked if it was the best result of his career, Hurzeler added: 'It is a difficult question to ask immediately after the game when the emotions are still high.

'It is very important to stay humble. We have to enjoy this moment, but understand why we had success, and come back to our roots which is about being brilliant in the basics,and trusting each other.'

Sports.title: Declan Rice loses his cool as Arsenal are thumped by Brighton: Frustrated Gunners star AVOIDS red card despite appearing to kick out at Malick Yalcouye as reason why he was not sent off is revealed
Sports.content:
Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice perhaps bizarrely avoided a red card against Brighton as the England midfielder lost his cool during his side's 3-0 defeat. The Premier League champions fell to a shock loss at the Seagulls – their first defeat of the season and first in the league since they became champions. Pascal Gross, Charalampos Kostoulas and Chema Andres were all on the scoresheet for the impressive hosts – but Rice caught the eye too. Brighton were seeing out the remainder of their game at the AMEX, with Rice trying to play out from the back under pressure from 20-year-old Malick Yalcouye. After the midfielder had passed the ball, his opponent gave him a shove, and the 27-year-old saw red – though not according to the referee. Rice hunted down Yalcouye, kicking out at the attacking midfielder, who fell to the ground. Declan Rice gets bodied, so has a tantrum and kicks the Brighton player… Any other player at any other club, that’s a straight red card and 3 match ban. Textbook. Never for Arsenal though! 😂 pic.twitter.com/d63kr6u8q1 — Football Confidential 🌐 (@footballconfid1) September 19, 2026 Declan Rice received backlash for kicking out at Brighton's Malick Yalcouye on Saturday The Arsenal midfielder lost his cool during his side's 3-0 defeat as he hunted his opponent down late on Brighton fans demanded a red card, with referee Darren England running in to cool things down as Yalcouye tried to confront the former West Ham captain. Fans were left bewildered as to why Rice wasn't given his marching orders, instead just given a yellow card by England. One posted on X: 'Seriously tho, HOW did Declan Rice not get sent off for this???? So far off the ball.' Another shared: 'No way Declan Rice didn't receive a red card for this tackle. Imagine it was Phil Foden.' As per talkSPORT, though, the decision was checked and cleared by VAR – because it did not meet the threshold for violent conduct. It was considered to be petulant and a yellow card was seen to be enough. Rice would have received a three-game ban had he seen a red card, meaning he would have missed games against Leeds, Nottingham Forest and Everton. Former FIFA referee and refs' chief Keith Hackett, meanwhile, feels Rice could have seen red - and likened the scenario to that that faced Phil Foden in the Manchester derby last week. 🚨 "It should have been 𝐑𝐄𝐃" - Ex-PGMOL chief @HACKETTREF says Declan Rice should have been sent off v Brighton as he makes Phil Foden comparison. Do you agree with him or has he got this one wrong? pic.twitter.com/atq0P4iQAx — Football Insider (@footyinsider247) September 19, 2026 He told Football Insider: 'Declan Rice, in a retaliatory action off the ball, kicks his opponent. He's fortunate the referee took a lenient view and saw it as reckless rather than violent conduct. 'Is the bar too high at Pro Ref? Last week we saw a situation where Bruno Fernandes kicked Phil Foden, who retaliated and received a red card. The Manchester United captain received nothing. 'In both these situations, you could determine that violent conduct could have taken place and red cards should have been issued. 'I suggest at Pro Ref they look at the incidents and determine where the bar stands in relation to kicking an opponent. '

Sports.title: Michael Carrick takes another swipe at referees after Erling Haaland's derby goal following huge VAR blunder - as Man United boss tells Howard Webb his apology 'doesn't mean an awful lot'
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick takes another swipe at referees after Erling Haaland's derby goal following huge VAR blunder - as Man United boss tells Howard Webb his apology 'doesn't mean an awful lot'

Michael Carrick says the apology from referees’ bosses for the VAR blunder over Erling Haaland’s goal in the Manchester derby ‘doesn’t mean an awful lot’.

Howard Webb, the head of Pro Ref, admitted the error after Haaland’s winner for Manchester City at Old Trafford last weekend was allowed to stand, even though his teammate Enzo Fernandez was in an offside position and clearly interfering with play.

Webb has blamed ‘tunnel vision’ for the mistake and stood down VAR officials Matt Donohue and Blake Antrobus until after the international break.

Carrick insists he still has faith in the system, but believes the best Manchester United can hope for now is that the marginal decisions will even themselves out over the course of the season.

‘Listen, one-off things can happen,’ he said as United prepare to return to Premier League action at Fulham on Sunday. ‘At the time it was a pretty big one, we know that. I don't think I need to go over that.

‘Yes, I've got faith in it, of course. It’s the system that we work towards and that we use, so the apology doesn't mean an awful lot.

Michael Carrick says Howard Webb's apology over Erling Haaland's goal 'doesn't mean a lot'

Enzo Fernandez was allowed to interfere with play before the goal in a huge VAR blunder

Webb has blamed 'tunnel vision' for the mistake and temporarily stood down the VAR officials

‘I can appreciate it and I respect them for putting their hands up and saying “we got that wrong”. It happens.

‘Moving forward, we just have to deal with what's thrown in front of us. Maybe we get one or two decisions on the back of how it balances out; percentages or law of averages or whatever that may be.’

Carrick has urged his players to put the controversy behind them and focus on recovering from a poor start to the season after losing half of their six games in all competitions.

‘That was a pretty big one to take and had a huge impact on that game, and that's why it was particularly tough,’ he added.

‘It can have an impact in that moment of time – it can have a big impact – but we can't let it have an impact on the rest of the season. That's for us to get back to winning ways as soon as possible.’

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney 'is in advanced talks with I'm A Celebrity bosses in show's biggest ever signing' two years after wife Coleen secured £1.5million for her stint
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney 'is in advanced talks with I'm A Celebrity bosses in show's biggest ever signing' two years after wife Coleen secured £1.5million for her stint

Wayne Rooney could follow in his wife Coleen's footsteps as he is said to be in advanced talks with I'm A Celebrity bosses to appear in this year's series.

According to reports, the former footballer, 40, would secure the biggest fee in the show's 24-year history – more than Coleen, 40, who made a record-breaking £1.5million for her jungle stint two years ago.

Last year, Wayne spoke about how he wanted to appear on I'm A Celebrity.

He said: '[I'm A Celebrity] is something I would never say no to, of course. I think I said on the aftershow when Coleen was in the jungle, that was the one we've always watched and the one we both said if there was anything we'd do it'd be that.

'So, you never know in the future, but I've got other things I'm looking at at the minute.'

Now TV insiders say he is keen to head to the jungle and impress his four sons.

Wayne Rooney could follow in his wife Coleen's footsteps as he is said to be in advanced talks with I'm A Celebrity bosses to appear in this year's series

'Wayne wants to show their sons what their dad can do and has joked he’ll be giving Coleen a run for her money. He is really competitive and hates losing so will give I’m A Celebrity his all.

It comes as the Rooney family are looking forward to the future and the release of their £10million fly-on-the-wall documentary.

The Real Rooneys will follow Wayne as he steps away from football management and swaps the touchline for school runs, while Coleen capitalises on the success of her I'm A Celebrity stint.

The teaser started with Wayne joking: 'This is my series,' to which Coleen hit back: 'Are you glad that I let you come on?'

Keeping up the banter, Wayne replied: 'Oh, here we go. Get over it!'

As their four boys piled onto the sofa, the WAG added: 'It's hectic, it's mad. Not much peace and quiet around here.

Sports.title: Pat McAfee roasted by his ESPN co-stars after he sparked furious backlash by 'smoking weed' live on air
Sports.content:
Pat McAfee roasted by his ESPN co-stars after he sparked furious backlash by 'smoking weed' live on air

Pat McAfee was trolled by his College GameDay co-stars after sparking fury this week by 'smoking weed' on ESPN.

During Thursday's episode of his eponymous ESPN/YouTube show, the 39-year-old punter-turned-talk show host was standing at his microphone during the second hour of the program – only this time he had what appeared to be a cigarette or joint in his left hand.

McAfee then rested the smoldering item on an ash tray in the same inconspicuous manner tobacco smokers Johnny Carson and Edward R Murrow did during their broadcast careers.

Fans quickly flooded social media to accuse McAfee of smoking pot during the show.

And although he has previously told the All the Smoke podcast he does smoke 'a lot of weed,' McAfee appeared to downplay the visual online by claiming he was actually burning an unintoxicating herb.

'Little sage never hurt nobody,' McAfee wrote on X before engaging in a few humorous exchanges with his followers. 'The ones who watch the progrum know it's either sage or cbd,' one follower wrote on X, prompting a 'THANK YOU' from McAfee.

Pat McAfee was trolled by his College GameDay co-stars after 'smoking weed' on ESPN

Legendary Alabama coach Nick Saban joked about McAfee's antics that set the internet ablaze

Per his usual, McAfee was standing at his microphone during the second hour of the program – only this time he had what appeared to be a cigarette or joint in his left hand

Despite that, McAfee's co-stars Nick Saban and Kirk Herbstreit took the opportunity to mock him for the scandal during Saturday's show from the campus of Ole Miss.

'Coach, have you ever used any, like, ancient medicine to potentially calm the boys? Like maybe burn some sage? You know what I'm talking about? Cause I've done that. Keep the bad spirits, keep the anxiety [away],' McAfee said to Saban.

'You do that in the studio! Just calm the lads down,' Kirk Herbstreit said to McAfee.

Then Saban interrupted and added: 'I actually think if we had some of your gummies, we would have won more games.'

Hemp-derived CBD is legal in Indiana, where the former Indianapolis Colts punter produces his show, but recreational marijuana remains banned in the state.

Possession of the drug in Indiana is punishable by up to 180 days behind bars and a potential fine of $1,000 for a first offense.

McAfee has made playful references to smoking pot and once appeared to take a hit off a vape pen during a live, public ESPN taping.

Viewers weren't necessarily shocked by Thursday's moment, but a few claimed McAfee would go unpunished where others might suffer consequences under similar circumstances.

'Pat McAfee is the most powerful person other than Donald Trump,' ex-Philadelphia Eagles running back LeSean McCoy said on his podcast, SpeakEasy. 'He's the only dude I know that can smoke weed on a show and nothing happens.'

'I'm not mad at it, but a long list of people not named Pat McAfee would probably be punished/fired for this,' wrote Eagles blogger Alexis Chassen.

'We all know if Pat McAfee was black,' another X user began, 'this never happens. I'm not saying it's about race, but I had to point that out... Paul Pierce got fired while off the clock doing the same thing.'

Pierce, the legendary Boston Celtics forward, was fired by ESPN in 2021 after posting video of himself on Instagram smoking, drinking and gambling with exotic dancers.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
